behavior.text: WHILE orientation is vertical and a tab's label is wider than its tab less the padding of the row's size on each side (and, beside an icon, less the icon and comp.tabs.container.gap) — a column narrower than its widest tab — THE tabs SHALL truncate the label at the end of its own direction (TAB-33) with an ellipsis, on one line, and SHALL show it whole as TAB-25 says.
behavior.verify: `vertical` in a tab list 120 wide: the longer labels end in an ellipsis, each tab is 120 wide, and hovering one shows its whole label in a tooltip.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the selected tab, and from it into its panel or, where the row has no panel, to whatever follows the row.
Horizontal: moves focus to the next or previous enabled tab, wrapping, and selects it (mirrored in right-to-left layouts). Vertical: does nothing.
Vertical: moves focus to the next or previous enabled tab, wrapping, and selects it. Horizontal: does nothing (the page scrolls).
Moves focus to the first or last enabled tab and selects it.
Selects the focused tab (needed only after the product has moved focus without selecting).
Cancels a drag that a pointer has in progress; the indicator returns to the selected tab and nothing is selected.

accessibility.labeling: Each tab is named by its label, drawn or not (labelHidden), and whole even when it is drawn truncated. The row is named by its own label. The selected tab's panel is named by its tab; a row with no panel names nothing but itself and its tabs. Icons, the covered copies of labels and icons, the track, the indicator, the underline and the divider are decorative.
notes: Activation is automatic: moving focus with the arrow keys selects the tab, as the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern recommends when a panel shows without a noticeable delay. A product whose panels load slowly shows a loading state in the panel; a manual mode (focus first, Enter to select) can be added later as a new prop without breaking this spec.

Tabs and the switch share one model: a thumb on a track that slides to what is chosen and follows a finger. A switch has two states, and its track, outline and handle differ between them; tabs have two or more equal choices, so their track never changes and the active indicator alone moves.

The drag is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.7): every tab is selected by a single tap or click on it, and by the arrow keys. With a screen reader running, a one-finger drag belongs to the reader; tabs are then selected by the reader's activation, as before.

A drag changes what is drawn, continuously (the indicator's place and width, and the labels' colors under it), and nothing that assistive technology is told: no tab is exposed as selected on the way, no panel changes, and no change is emitted for the tabs the indicator passes (TAB-30). There is no threshold in the look; the place where two tabs meet decides only what a release chooses.
Selection is the row's: value holds the selected tab's value, and change carries the new one. A tab's disabled is its own.

Web: `tanrei-tab-panel` elements are matched to tabs by their `value` attribute, whether they are the row's children or a linked `tanrei-tab-view`'s, and get role tabpanel, aria-labelledby and the tab's aria-controls. SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter and React Native have no tab panel role; there the selected panel follows the row in reading order, and each README says so.
Tabs switch views of one subject. Moving between destinations of an app belongs to the navigation bar or drawer.

A Tab view (`tab-view`) draws its own row of tabs from its panels by default, or is linked to a row placed elsewhere; either way it holds the panels. The link is by value: the Tab view shows the panel of `value`, follows the tabs when a tab is selected, and sets `value` on both and emits its own change when the user swipes it (TBV-2, TBV-4). While a swipe is in progress it sets `indicatorOffset`, which places the active indicator and the underline between two tabs (TAB-26); TAB-24 makes the covered colors follow the indicator wherever it is drawn. A drag across the row and a swipe of the view are one gesture in two places: the indicator follows the finger, the selection is made on release (from halfway, or by a fling), a cancelled gesture returns it, and nothing is announced before the release. They differ in reach: a swipe moves one panel, and the panels travel with it; a drag across the row can pass several tabs, and the panels wait for the release, then switch as for a selected tab (TBV-2). A row without a Tab view shows its own panels (TAB-13).

Text size never hides a label: a tab that hugs its content grows wider and the row scrolls; a tab that shares the row's width truncates its label, which stays the tab's accessible name and is shown whole where the platform can (TAB-25). A product whose labels are long, translated, written by users, or read at large text sizes keeps the default hug.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

A shared choice (group) is one decision shown in many places: a person who picks a platform, a language or a unit once should not be asked again by every sample on the page. The rows that follow change silently and at once (TAB-38): nothing is announced, focus stays on the tab the person used, and each row tells assistive technology its selected tab when the person reaches it. A change of content elsewhere on the page is not a change of context (WCAG 3.2.2), but it should not surprise: rows of one group carry the same labels for the same values (WCAG 3.2.4), and a product whose rows are far apart says near the first one that the choice applies to the whole page.

Tabs of different rows are matched by value, never by label, so a choice survives a translated label, an icon-only tab and a change of wording, and a remembered choice still holds after the person changes language.

Remembering (rememberAs) is off unless the product names a key, and what is kept is one short string the product itself wrote as a tab's value: no text a person typed, no identifier, nothing sent anywhere by the component. Whether keeping a preference on the device needs the person's consent where the product is used is the product's to decide, which is why there is no default key and no remembering by default. A person who blocks storage loses nothing but the memory (TAB-39).

The page does not move under the person (TAB-40): a row whose choice changes the height of samples above it stays under the pointer and under keyboard focus, which is what WCAG 2.4.3 and 3.2.2 ask of a control that changes content elsewhere, and what keeps a person using magnification from losing their place.

A row without panels (TAB-42) is still tabs when the choice changes what is shown below the row: Day, Week and Month over a calendar; Standard, Medium and High over the examples of a page; a unit over a table. It is announced as a tab list whose tabs control nothing, so the row's label is what tells a person what they are choosing, and the product draws the result after the row in reading order where it can, so that a person who has chosen finds it by reading on; where the choice reaches the whole page, the label or the words beside the row say so. A choice that sets a value sent with a form, or that changes nothing a person can see, is not tabs: it is radio buttons.

Variant, track, size and transition say how the row looks and moves, never what it is: every combination is a tab list with one keyboard model (TAB-49, TAB-50). Primary is the row of a screen's main views, secondary a row inside one of them, tonal the quiet row — in the heading of a sample, in a header, in a toolbar — where the choice should not draw the eye from what it changes.

The selected tab is told to assistive technology as a state, and to sight by the indicator and by its label. A tonal row's indicator is a quiet mark on purpose: in the default system a layer about 1.4:1 from what it lies on, the same step on the track and on any surface, with the selected label darker than the others. It is not held to 3:1 against its ground, as the selected destination of a navigation drawer is not. A person who needs more has the system's medium and high contrast and the platform's forced colors, where the indicator is a filled highlight (TAB-45); a product that cannot accept the quiet mark uses secondary or primary, which are filled.

Without its track (TAB-49) a row has no ground of its own: its labels are held on every surface role of the system, and a product that places a row on a color of its own checks the labels against it, as it does for text.

A small row (TAB-44) is 32 tall and still pressed over the minimum target (TAB-5, WCAG 2.5.8): its hit area reaches above and below it, which a header or a toolbar has room for. Directly over content that answers a press at its top edge, that content wins the overlap; a product that stacks a small row tight against such content uses the medium size.

transition none (TAB-43) takes away the motion the row plays by itself when the selection changes, in every motion setting; it takes away no way of selecting, and a drag across the row still carries the indicator under the finger. Where motion is reduced every row is drawn that way, and the state colors then change at once too (TAB-23), a ripple appearing whole (TAB-9).

A vertical tab list (orientation vertical) is still tabs: one subject's views, the categories of a settings page or the sections of one record, with the arrow keys of its axis (Down and Up). It is not a menu of destinations — moving between the pages of an app belongs to the navigation drawer, whose items are links. A column never wraps a label: a column narrower than its widest tab truncates the label, which stays the tab's whole name, and shows it whole in a tooltip (TAB-61).

WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on the row's host THE tabs SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on the element that carries the row's role (its tab list) — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it. WHEN the product removes the aria- attribute or its data-aria- twin THE tabs SHALL take it off that element. A tab's host carries the tab's role itself, so what the product writes on it is not moved.

tab.notes: A child element: `<tanrei-tab value="overview" label="Overview" icon="dashboard">`, with `label-hidden` and `disabled` attributes, as `<option>` in a `<select>`.

web.notes: `tanrei-tabs` (variant, full-width, value, label) holds `tanrei-tab` children and, after them, `tanrei-tab-panel` children matched to tabs by their `value` attribute, or is drawn by a `tanrei-tab-view` as its own row, or is named by a linked `tanrei-tab-view` (`tabs="<id>"`) whose `tanrei-tab-panel` children take their place. `indicatorOffset` is a property only, with no attribute: the Tab view writes it in every frame of a drag. `value` names the selected tab, as a `<select>`'s does. It sets role tablist, tab and tabpanel, aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby, hides the panels that are not selected, and gives a panel with no focusable content tabindex 0. It sets its own `value` before firing `change`, as a native control does. The covered copy of a label and icon (TAB-24) is an `aria-hidden` layer clipped with `clip-path` to the indicator's box, animated with it; a truncated label (`text-overflow: ellipsis`) shows the whole label in a plain tooltip (TAB-25) without `aria-describedby`, since it is already the name. The track is the row's own background, and the tabs scroll inside it. A drag (TAB-28 to TAB-30) is followed with Pointer Events: `pointerdown` on the row, `setPointerCapture` once the drag is taken, `pointermove` placing the indicator, `pointerup` choosing the tab, and `pointercancel`, `lostpointercapture` or Escape cancelling; the `click` that follows a taken drag is swallowed, and `aria-selected` is written only on the release. The in-between look needs no second mechanism: the indicator's inset and width are the same custom properties a slide transitions, written in each frame of a drag, and the covered copy's `clip-path` follows them, so a drag and a slide draw the same frames. `touch-action: pan-y` on a row that does not scroll (and on the selected tab of one that does) leaves sideways drags to the row and vertical ones to the page. A shared choice: `group` and `remember-as` are attributes with the properties `group` and `rememberAs`. A group is the `tanrei-tabs` of one document that name it, those inside shadow trees and those a `tanrei-tab-view` drew included; an iframe is another document. The members and the choice are kept by the module, in a map from the name, and never in the DOM. `remember-as` is a key of the origin's `localStorage`, read synchronously before the row's first render and at most once for each key, every access inside `try`, so a browser that blocks storage or throws on it costs nothing but the memory; a key is the product's to namespace, since `localStorage` is shared by everything on the origin. A member that follows is written (`value`, `aria-selected`, its panels' `hidden`) with its slide and its color transition off for that frame. For TAB-40 the row acted on reads its `getBoundingClientRect().top` before the group is written and once more after, and moves `scrollTop` of its nearest scrolling ancestor (the document's scrolling element where none is nearer) by the difference with `behavior: 'instant'`; a browser that anchors scrolling itself has by then moved some or all of the way, and the row corrects only what is left, so the two never add up. `change` bubbles, so one listener on the document hears each choice once and reads the group from `event.target.group`. The first frame of TAB-39 is the first the element draws: before `tanrei-tabs` is defined the element draws nothing of its own, and a product that shows server-rendered rows before then guards that as it guards any element not yet defined. The value `tonal` of `variant`; `size` is an attribute and a property (`small`, `medium`); both axes are open registries (`TanreiTabsVariantRegistry`, `TanreiTabsSizeRegistry` in `registry.ts`, in the Button's form), and each size's five tokens are read through the same private custom properties, set by a block per size as a variant's are. A small row's tab keeps its 32-high box and carries the hit area of TAB-5 as an inset pseudo-element that reaches above and below it, under any interactive content it overlaps; the row itself is not made taller. `track` is a property that is true, false or null: the attribute is absent for null, present for true and `="false"` for false, as the tooltip's `arrow` is; null reads `--tanrei-comp-tabs-track-visible` from the cascade by a style query, as a separation is read, and off sets the track's fill to none and nothing else. `transition` is an attribute and a property (`auto`, `slide`, `none`); auto reads `--tanrei-comp-tabs-motion-transition`, in the stylesheet by a style query and once in the script for the scroll and the settle after a drag; under none the indicator's and the cover's transitions and the selected look's color transition are off, `scrollIntoView` uses `behavior: 'instant'`, and the drag is taken as it is under `prefers-reduced-motion`. The tonal indicator is one element with a translucent background, so its slide and resize never overlap two drawings of it (TAB-50). A row without panels (TAB-42) writes no `aria-controls` and is what the element already is when it has no `tanrei-tab-panel`.

tab.notes: `TanreiTab(value, label, icon, labelHidden, enabled)` called in the `TanreiTabs { }` content lambda. `enabled` is the inverse flag.

compose.notes: `TanreiTabs(selectedValue, onSelectedValueChange, variant, fullWidth, contentDescription) { TanreiTab(…) }`, one composable for rows that hug and rows that fill (Material's `PrimaryTabRow`, `SecondaryTabRow` and `ScrollableTabRow` in one). State hoisting: the caller keeps `selectedValue` and moves it from `onSelectedValueChange`. A truncated label (`maxLines = 1`, `TextOverflow.Ellipsis`) is shown whole in a plain tooltip on long press and hover (TAB-25). Compose has no tab panel role: the product shows the selected tab's content below the row. Until it catches up it ships `scrollable` instead of `fullWidth`, a line indicator and wrapping fixed labels. `link` is the shared `rememberTanreiTabLink()` a linked Tab view is passed too: the tabs read the indicator offset (TAB-26) from it and report their order and disabled tabs to the Tab view through it; without a Tab view it is omitted and the offset is 0. The drag is `Modifier.pointerInput` with `detectHorizontalDragGestures` (or `draggable` with a `DraggableState`) on the row, a `VelocityTracker` giving the fling; `onSelectedValueChange` is called only when the drag ends. Until it catches up it also draws no track and follows no drag. A shared choice has no parameter here: rows given the same hoisted `selectedValue` show the same choice, which is the group (TAB-36), and recompose in one frame. The caller gives a row that lacks a value a state of its own, since a selection that names none of a row's tabs selects none (TAB-11), and remembers by keeping the state in DataStore or `SharedPreferences`, read before the first composition. TAB-37 to TAB-41 describe a group the component keeps, which this platform does not have: every row slides as TAB-17 says for a value the product sets, since the row cannot tell following from being set; the README says so, and says that a `LazyColumn` keeps its first visible item in place when items above change height while a scrolling `Column` does not. Not built on this platform yet: the selected label's added weight from `selected.label.emphasis` with every tab keeping the heavier label's width (TAB-16, TAB-50); the selected tab's state layer over its active indicator (TAB-18); the icon's place read from `icon.placement` of the row's size (TAB-18); `TanreiTabsVariant.Tonal`; `size: TanreiTabsSize` (`Small`, `Medium`); `track: Boolean? = null` (null reads the generated choice `trackVisible`); `transition: TanreiTabsTransition` (`Auto`, `Slide`, `None`), under `None` the indicator is placed with `snapTo` in place of `animateTo` and the drag is still detected. The hit area of a small row is `Modifier.minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` outside the drawn box.

tab.name: TanreiTab
tab.notes: `TanreiTab<T>(value:, label:, icon:, labelHidden:, enabled:)` widgets in the bar's `tabs:` list.

flutter.notes: `TanreiTabBar<T>(value:, onChanged:, variant:, isScrollable:, semanticLabel:, tabs: [TanreiTab<T>(…)])`, as `TabBar` but selected by value rather than by a `TabController`'s index; the caller moves `value` from `onChanged`. `isScrollable` is the inverse of fullWidth, as in Flutter's `TabBar`, and defaults to true (hug). A truncated label (`maxLines: 1`, `TextOverflow.ellipsis`) is shown whole in a `Tooltip` (TAB-25). `TanreiTabBarView` gives way to the Tab view, `TanreiTabView`, which draws a `TanreiTabBar` itself or is linked by `link:`, a `TanreiTabLink<T>` passed to both, as Flutter's `TabController` is shared by a `TabBar` and a `TabBarView`: the bar reads the indicator offset (TAB-26) from it and reports its order and disabled tabs to the view through it. Until it catches up, `TanreiTabBarView<T>(value:, children:, semanticLabels:)` shows the panel of the selected value and does not swipe. Until it catches up it ships `isScrollable` defaulting to false, a line indicator and wrapping fixed labels. The drag is a `GestureDetector`'s `onHorizontalDragStart`, `onHorizontalDragUpdate` and `onHorizontalDragEnd` on the bar, `DragEndDetails.primaryVelocity` giving the fling; `onChanged` is called only from `onHorizontalDragEnd`. Until it catches up it also draws no track and follows no drag. A shared choice has no parameter here: bars given the same `value` from one piece of the product's state show the same choice, which is the group (TAB-36), and rebuild in one frame. The product gives a bar that lacks a value a state of its own, since a selection that names none of a bar's tabs selects none (TAB-11), and remembers with `shared_preferences` or its own store, read before the first build. TAB-37 to TAB-41 describe a group the component keeps, which this platform does not have: every row slides as TAB-17 says for a value the product sets, since the row cannot tell following from being set; the README says so, and says that a scroll view does not hold a bar in place when content above it changes height. Not built on this platform yet: the selected label's added weight from `selected.label.emphasis` with every tab keeping the heavier label's width (TAB-16, TAB-50); the selected tab's state layer over its active indicator (TAB-18); the icon's place read from `icon.placement` of the row's size (TAB-18); `TanreiTabsVariant.tonal`; `size: TanreiTabsSize` (`small`, `medium`); `bool? track` (null reads the generated choice `trackVisible`); `transition: TanreiTabsTransition` (`auto`, `slide`, `none`), under `none` the controller's value is set without `animateTo` and the horizontal drag is still recognised. The hit area of a small row is a `GestureDetector` box of the minimum target with `HitTestBehavior.translucent`.

react-native.name: Tabs

tab.name: Tab
tab.notes: The element type of the row's `items` array: `{ value, label, icon?, labelHidden?, disabled? }`.

react-native.notes: `<Tabs items={Tab[]} value onValueChange variant fullWidth accessibilityLabel>`; controlled, the caller moves `value` from `onValueChange` and renders the selected panel below the row. The row has the `tablist` role and each tab the `tab` role with its selected state; React Native has no tab panel role, so the selected panel follows the row in reading order. A truncated label (`numberOfLines={1}`, `ellipsizeMode="tail"`) keeps the whole label as the tab's `accessibilityLabel`; React Native has no tooltip of its own, so it is not shown whole elsewhere (TAB-25: where the platform has an idiom). Until it catches up it ships `scrollable` instead of `fullWidth`, a line indicator and wrapping fixed labels. `link` is the shared `useTabLink()` a linked Tab view is passed too: the tabs read the indicator offset (TAB-26) from it and report their order and disabled tabs to the Tab view through it; without a Tab view it is omitted and the offset is 0. The drag is a `PanResponder` on the row (or React Native Gesture Handler's `Gesture.Pan()` where the product has it), claiming the responder once the drag passes the slop sideways, with the release's `vx` giving the fling; `onValueChange` is called only on release. Until it catches up it also draws no track and follows no drag. A shared choice has no prop here: rows given the same controlled `value` from one piece of the product's state show the same choice, which is the group (TAB-36), and render in one commit. The product gives a row that lacks a value a state of its own, since a selection that names none of a row's tabs selects none (TAB-11), and remembers with AsyncStorage or its own store; AsyncStorage answers after the first frame, so a product that must not show another tab first reads it before it mounts the screen. TAB-37 to TAB-41 describe a group the component keeps, which this platform does not have: every row slides as TAB-17 says for a value the product sets, since the row cannot tell following from being set; the README says so, and says that a `ScrollView` holds a row in place only with `maintainVisibleContentPosition`. Not built on this platform yet: the selected label's added weight from `selected.label.emphasis` with every tab keeping the heavier label's width (TAB-16, TAB-50); the selected tab's state layer over its active indicator (TAB-18); the icon's place read from `icon.placement` of the row's size (TAB-18); `variant="tonal"`; `size` (`"small"`, `"medium"`); `track?: boolean | null` (null reads the generated choice `trackVisible`); `transition` (`"auto"`, `"slide"`, `"none"`), under `"none"` the indicator's value is set with `setValue` in place of `Animated.timing` and the `PanResponder` stays. The hit area of a small row is `hitSlop`.
